thread:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] Elevated KMS decrypt/sign latency detected across multiple regions. Trigger: kms.decrypt.p95 > 1.2s for 5m. Affected: control-plane startup and request-signing paths. Paging on-call now.
Maya: Ack. Starting triage. Pulling control-plane logs, recent deploys, and canary health.
Samir: Traces show repeated RPC errors: `rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded` and some `Unavailable`. Regions: asia-southeast1 and europe-west1 most affected.
Eli: Running manual `gcloud kms decrypt` calls — seeing spikes to ~3s occasionally. No public GCP KMS outage posted. Could be regional control-plane congestion.
Maya: Impact so far: (1) Dedicated warm replicas failing init due to key unwrap timeouts; (2) Hosted API signing path 95th percentile latency spikes causing upstream request timeouts.
Riley: Support reports three enterprise tenants with failed model loads and one on-prem customer with repeated watchdog restarts. Open tickets: #2001, #2002, #2003.
Jordan: Categorize as potential Sev2 for Dedicated customers; need mitigation ASAP. Oncall, propose quick fixes.
Samir: Quick mitigation plan: (A) enable local ephemeral key cache during startup, (B) throttle concurrent KMS unwraps to avoid thundering herd, (C) enable cross-region key fallback for signing, (D) increase client timeouts/backoff.
Maya: Start with A+B. Samir, can you flip the `kms.startup_cache` flag on a small canary?
Samir: Flipped `kms.startup_cache=true` on canary cluster cp-canary-03. Monitoring.
OpsBot: Deploy started: control-plane/flags/kms.startup_cache by @Samir. Canary nodes: cp-canary-03a, cp-canary-03b.
Samir: Canary nodes bootstrapped successfully; cache prevented repeated unwraps and reduced KMS calls.
Eli: Preparing cross-region fallback but need IAM checks for target key. ETA ~8min. I'll validate service account permissions.
Maya: Also reduce startup concurrency: set `startup.max_concurrency=3` for affected pools to smooth load.
Riley: Drafting customer status update: "We're investigating increased KMS latency affecting instance startups and signing. Temporary mitigations deployed; customers may see improved behavior shortly. No data exposure." Approve to post?
Jordan: Post to affected tenants and update status page. Keep incident at P2 until recovery confirmed.
Eli: GCP Support replied: they observed elevated latencies for a subset of key rings in asia-southeast1 between 22:10-22:36 UTC due to backend scaling stress; they're rolling an internal fix.
Samir: After rolling cache and concurrency changes across pools, startup failure rate dropped to near zero and signing latency reverted toward baseline. Observability ingestion was delayed ~2-3m which made initial detection noisy.
Maya: Confirm mitigations applied: local cache enabled, startup concurrency throttled, client retry/backoff increased. Cross-region fallback staged but not needed after backend improvement.
Jordan: Handoff: I'm taking overnight watch. Maya, please attach runbook steps and list of config changes to the incident doc.
Maya: Done. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-mitigation (internal). Actions recorded in incident journal.
Riley: Customer comms updated and tickets annotated with timeline and mitigations. Scheduling EOD follow-up with impacted customers.
IncidentBot: Severity updated: Sev2 -> Sev3 after mitigations. Reminder: open postmortem and assign owners.
Maya: Postmortem action items: (1) default ephemeral local cache for startup path (@Eli), (2) add cross-region fallback tests to canary suite (@Samir), (3) tune KMS client retries/backoff defaults (@Samir), (4) add alert on KMS unwrap error rate and ingestion lag correlation (@Maya).
Samir: Owners acknowledged. I'll also add a chaos test simulating KMS high-latency to the smoke suite.
Jordan: Thanks team. I'll monitor overnight and escalate if GCP status updates indicate regression. Closing thread after handoff notes.
Maya: Closing on-call. Add any asynchronous notes below for Jordan.
Riley: Added customer follow-up notes and marked support loop as initial-mitigation-closed.
notes: No title included per agents.md requirements; thread is single continuous string with chronological messages.
